findings.title: memory-awareness DB recall has NO cheap-prompt cache: every qualifying prompt (>=15 chars, not slash) pays the full daemon-probe + 2 uv subprocesses, even for back-to-back identical or trivial intents — unlike heartbeat which has a 30s cache guard
findings.observe_how: Submit the same prompt twice; memory-recall.jsonl shows two full-cost fires (no dedupe/TTL). Contrast heartbeat.ts shouldUpdateHeartbeat 30s cache that skips the DB write.
findings.telemetry: memory-recall.jsonl logs one full-cost row per qualifying prompt regardless of repetition; no cache key recorded.

findings.title: Every Postgres-backed UserPromptSubmit hook pays uv-run cold start (~2.2s) PER QUERY: db-utils-pg.runPgQuery and memory-awareness both shell out to `uv run python` rather than holding a connection — the uv interpreter startup, not the SQL, is the dominant cost
findings.observe_how: Time `uv run python -c 'pass'` cold (~2s) vs the actual asyncpg.connect+query (~50-100ms on localhost); the ratio shows ~95% of heartbeat/recall DB latency is interpreter startup.
findings.telemetry: runPgQuery timeout is 3000ms (line 71); the comment 'reduced for faster startup' confirms uv startup is the bottleneck being fought, not query time.

coverage_manifest: heartbeat.ts: 1 Postgres-via-uv-run call (registerSession), gated by 30s file cache (shouldUpdateHeartbeat) — cheap on cache hit, ~2.2s uv startup on miss. Verdict: cached, low cost; cited as the GOOD pattern in D6a-07/D6a-08.
maestro-state-manager.ts: pure regex + lock'd file IO (readStateWithLock/writeStateWithLock), 1-in-100 cleanup. No subprocess/DB/network. Verdict: cheap.
guardrail-enforcer.ts: pure regex over 3 guardrails + tmp session-state file read/write. No subprocess. Verdict: cheap.
skill-activation-prompt.ts: spawns `uv run python -c` pattern_inference on EVERY non-empty prompt (2s timeout, ~2.2s uv startup) + skill-rules.json parse + graph resolution. Verdict: HEAVY — D6a-03.
bus-session-populator.ts: mutateBus (200ms lock cap, file write) + sanitize. No subprocess/network. Verdict: cheap (bounded by bus lock).

memory-awareness.ts: daemon TCP probe (1500ms) + checkLocalMemory uv (2s) + checkDbMemory uv (5-12s) SEQUENTIALLY + awaited Braintrust HTTP (2-4s) + readBus + intel-bus append. Verdict: DOMINANT hot-path cost — D6a-01/02/06/07/08; SEED-08.
maestro-detector.ts: pure regex complexity scoring + maestro-state.json statSync. No subprocess. Verdict: cheap.

user-confirmation-detector.ts: regex match; on confirmation/memory phrase fires execSync `uv run python store_learning.py` shell:true timeout 60000 SYNCHRONOUSLY. Verdict: conditional 60s stall — D6a-04 (latency angle of D5a-03/SEED-01).
ralph-watchdog.ts: readRalphUnifiedState (JSON file) + early-exit if no active Ralph. No subprocess. Verdict: cheap.
ralph-progress-inject.ts: readRalphUnifiedState + optional .vercel/project.json existsSync + tmp reminded-file IO. Self-warns >100ms. No DB/network. Verdict: cheap.
ralph-retry-reminder.ts: readRalphUnifiedState + early-exit if no active Ralph/empty retry queue. spawnSync imported but unused in the path. Verdict: cheap.
braintrust_hooks.py user_prompt_submit (13th hook): full Python interpreter spawn, 10s budget. Verdict: per-prompt Python cold-start tax — D6a-05.

sentry-error-context.ts: SECOND UserPromptSubmit block = extra process spawn; no-op via SENTRY env early-exit (D6a-09) AND reads wrong field user_message vs prompt (D6a-10). Verdict: dead weight + latent bug.

shared/db-utils-pg.ts runPgQuery: ALL coordination Postgres queries go through spawnSync('uv','run','python') — uv cold start ~2.2s dominates over ~50-100ms SQL. Verdict: structural cost driver — D6a-08.

shared/embedding-client.ts isDaemonReady: readDaemonInfo + isDaemonAlive(process.kill,0) + pingDaemon TCP (1500ms budget). Cheap when daemon up; on miss fire-and-forget ensureDaemonRunning (detached, non-blocking). Verdict: bounded 1500ms probe on the recall path.

shared/braintrust-score.ts emitBraintrustScore: 2x fetch with AbortSignal.timeout(2000) — project lookup (cold cache) + feedback POST, both awaited by memory-awareness. Verdict: up to 4s network on critical path — D6a-06; SEED-16.
notes:
TOP-5 LATENCY CONTRIBUTORS (worst-case serial, UserPromptSubmit), all VERIFIED:
1. memory-awareness.ts (DOMINANT): daemon probe 1.5s + checkLocalMemory uv 2s + checkDbMemory uv 5-12s + Braintrust HTTP 2-4s, run SEQUENTIALLY (memory-awareness.ts:586-587, :151-162, :225-240, :656-660). SEED-08 measured 13-17s for this leg alone. The docstring's "in parallel" (line 13) is FALSE — main() awaits each in order.
2. user-confirmation-detector.ts: conditional execSync store_learning.py, timeout 60000, shell:true, on the prompt-submit path (:129-141). Only fires on 'fixed/it works/remember this' but a single such prompt can stall ~60s if DB is slow.
3. skill-activation-prompt.ts: `uv run python -c` pattern inference on EVERY prompt, 2s timeout (~2.2s uv cold start) (:206-212, :384).
4. braintrust_hooks.py user_prompt_submit: full Python interpreter cold-start, 10s budget (settings.json:237-241).
5. heartbeat.ts registerSession: ~2.2s uv-run Postgres on cache miss (heartbeat.ts:87; db-utils-pg.ts:68-71) — but gated by a 30s cache, so amortized cheap.

WORST-CASE SERIAL STACK at UserPromptSubmit (qualifying prompt, daemon cold, caches cold, confirmation phrase present): ~1.5 (daemon probe) + 2 (local uv) + 12 (db uv hybrid) + 4 (braintrust lookup+POST) + 2 (skill-activation uv) + 2 (heartbeat uv) + ~3 (braintrust_hooks.py python) + 60 (user-confirmation store_learning) + ~1s (10 Node interpreter cold-starts @ ~50-100ms) ≈ 22s typical / up to ~85s if the 60s confirmation timeout trips. TYPICAL (no confirmation, daemon warm, heartbeat cached): ~6-9s, dominated by checkDbMemory hybrid recall (5-12s, SEED-08). Claude Code runs all hooks in one event's array; the per-hook `timeout` values in settings.json are independent ceilings, not a shared budget — the 13 UserPromptSubmit timeouts sum to ~76s of allowable serial wait.

memory-awareness EARLY-EXIT / FIRE GUARDS (where the 13-17s recall is SKIPPED), VERIFIED at memory-awareness.ts:507-534:
- CLAUDE_AGENT_ID set (subagent) -> outputContinue, NO recall (line 507-510). This is why 30/36 agents never recall (subagents are skipped by design).
- prompt.length < 15 -> skip (513-516).
- prompt.trim().startsWith('/') (slash command) -> skip (519-522).
- extractIntent(prompt).length < 3 -> skip (531-534).
If NONE of these trip, the full recall fires unconditionally (no per-prompt result cache — D6a-07), so back-to-back identical prompts each pay full cost. Note the guards are length/slash only — they do NOT filter <task-notification> XML blobs, which is why those become recall intents (SEED-13 / D4a-09 intent pollution) AND each pays full recall cost.

PRE-TOOLUSE hot path (typical Edit): plan-to-ralph-enforcer + file-claims fire on Edit|Write. file-claims.mjs -> checkFileClaim/claimFile -> runPgQuery (uv-run Postgres, ~2.2s each, db-utils-pg.ts:594-695) = up to 2 uv subprocesses per Edit. acquireLockSync busy-waits (D2a-10, sibling dim). On a typical Edit the Postgres-via-uv file-claim is the dominant cost (~2-4s); the other PreToolUse Edit hooks (plan-to-ralph-enforcer) are file-IO only. The PostToolUse Edit|Write chain is heavier still (git-auto-commit, post-edit-diagnostics 35s budget, tree-invalidate, pageindex-watch, import-validator) but that is outside D6a's UserPromptSubmit/Edit-PreToolUse scope and overlaps D2/D3 dimensions.

Cross-dim: D6a-04 is the LATENCY characterization of the SAME execSync that D5a-03 flags for injection and SEED-01 flags for junk creation — not a duplicate, a third (perf) facet of one root cause (the un-pooled, shell:true store_learning subprocess in a hot-path hook). The structural root for D6a-01/03/05/08 is identical: CCv3 hooks have no long-lived worker/connection pool — every DB or Python need re-pays `uv run` (~2.2s) or `python` interpreter cold-start, multiplied across 13 serial UserPromptSubmit processes.
